In 1948 Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia granted land at Shashamane, in the south of the country, to black people from the West who wished to return to Africa. Rastafari settlers from Jamaica later made it their home, and the town still has a Rastafari community.

The grant was a thank-you to people of African descent abroad who had rallied to Ethiopia when Fascist Italy invaded it in the Second Italo-Ethiopian War of 1935. It was made through the Ethiopian World Federation, set up in New York to support Ethiopia.

For Rastafari, who see Haile Selassie as divine and Ethiopia as the promised land, the grant answered an old dream of return that went back to Marcus Garvey. A few settlers came in the 1950s, and more after the emperor visited Jamaica in 1966.

The settlement stayed small. After the emperor fell in 1974, the Derg took much of the land in its reforms. Today a few hundred Rastafari live there.
